question: How long will I wait for a decision if I extend my Student visa from inside the UK?
expected: Usually within 8 weeks

rag.answer: If you extend your Student visa from inside the UK, you will usually get a decision within 8 weeks [1, 5]. You may also be able to pay to get a faster decision [1, 5].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Apply online > Apply inside the UK
Student visa > Extend your visa > How long it takes to get a decision

closed_book.answer: If you apply to extend your Student visa from inside the UK, you will usually get a decision within 8 weeks. This 8-week period starts from the day you attend your biometric appointment at a UK Visa and Citizenship Application Services (UKVCAS) service point, or the day you submit your identity via the 'UK Immigration: ID Check' app. Faster processing options, such as priority or super priority services, may be available for an extra fee to get a decision sooner.

question: I'm 16. Am I old enough to get a Student visa?
expected: Yes, you can apply from 16, but you need your parents' consent at 16 or 17, and you may be eligible for a Child Student visa instead

rag.answer: Yes, you are old enough because you can apply for a Student visa if you are 16 or over [1]. However, because you are 16, you will also need consent from your parents and evidence of this when you apply [1].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview

closed_book.answer: Yes, you can apply for a Student visa if you are 16 or 17 years old. However, if you are 16 or 17, you will need written consent from your parents or legal guardians confirming the application, your living arrangements, and your travel to the UK.

question: I'm already in the UK on another visa. How early can I apply for my Student visa?
expected: Up to 3 months before the course starts, and before your current visa expires; the new course must start within 28 days of your current visa expiring

rag.answer: The earliest you can apply to switch to a Student visa is 3 months before your course starts [3].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Switch to this visa > When to apply

closed_book.answer: If you are already in the UK on another visa and want to switch to a Student visa, you can apply at any time before your current visa expires. However, you must apply before your current permission to stay runs out to avoid overstaying.

question: How early can I fly to the UK before my course starts?
expected: Up to 1 month before if the course lasts more than 6 months, up to 1 week before if 6 months or less, and never before the start date on your visa

rag.answer: You can arrive before your course starts either up to 1 week before if your course lasts 6 months or less, or up to 1 month before if your course lasts more than 6 months [3]. However, you must not travel to the UK before the start date given on your visa, regardless of when your course starts [3].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview > How long you can stay

closed_book.answer: How early you can travel to the UK depends on the length of your course. If your course is 6 months or longer, you can arrive up to 1 month before the course start date. If your course is shorter than 6 months, you can arrive up to 7 days before the course start date. These rules apply regardless of when you apply for your Student visa.

question: How much do I have to pay to apply for a Student visa?
expected: £558, plus the healthcare surcharge

rag.answer: It costs £558 to apply for a Student visa from outside the UK, or to extend or switch to a Student visa from inside the UK [1]. You must also pay the healthcare surcharge as part of your application, the cost of which depends on how long your visa lasts [1].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview > Fees

closed_book.answer: To apply for a Student visa from outside the UK, the standard fee is £490 per person. If you are applying to switch to or extend a Student visa from inside the UK, the standard fee is also £490 per person. You will also need to pay the Immigration Health Surcharge as part of your application.

question: How much money do I need in my bank account to study in Manchester?
expected: £1,171 a month for up to 9 months (outside London), held for at least 28 days in a row, plus the first year's course fees

rag.answer: To study in Manchester, which is outside London, you will need £1,171 per month (for up to 9 months) to support yourself [1]. You also need enough money to pay for your course for 1 academic year, the amount of which will be on your CAS [1, 5]. You must have held this money for at least 28 days in a row, ending within 31 days of your application [1]. However, you do not need to prove you have this money if you have been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months on the date of your application [1, 5].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Money you need > Money to support yourself (‘financial requirement’)
Student visa > Money you need > Course fee

closed_book.answer: To study in Manchester, you generally need enough money to cover your course fees for one academic year (up to 9 years) plus living costs. For a course in Manchester, the living costs requirement is £1,023 per month for up to 9 months, meaning you will need a maximum of £9,207 for living costs. You must hold these funds in your bank account for at least 28 consecutive days, ending no more than 31 days before your application date.

question: I'm Canadian. Do I have to take an English test for my Student visa?
expected: No, Canadian nationals do not need to prove their English

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: If you are a national of Canada, you do not need to prove your knowledge of English for a Student visa, as Canada is recognized as a majority English-speaking country by the UK. Your Canadian passport is sufficient to meet the English language requirement.

question: What English level do I need for a Student visa if I'm doing a degree?
expected: CEFR level B2 (B1 for courses below degree level)

rag.answer: If you are studying at degree level or above, you must prove your level of English is equivalent to CEFR level B2 [3]. Your Higher Education Provider can assess your level of English themselves if you are studying at this level [3].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Knowledge of English > Passing an English test

closed_book.answer: If you are studying at degree level or above, you generally need to prove you have the B2 level of English, which is equivalent to CEFR level B2. If you are studying below degree level, you usually need to prove you have CEFR level B1. Your education provider may assess your level themselves, so the exact requirement can vary depending on your course and sponsor.

question: My university sent me my CAS 7 months ago. Can I still use it to apply?
expected: No, you must apply within 6 months of receiving your CAS

rag.answer: You must apply for a Student visa within 6 months of getting a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) [2, 3]. Because your university sent you your CAS 7 months ago, you cannot use it to apply [2, 3].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Extend your visa > When to apply
Student visa > Switch to this visa > When to apply

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot use a Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies (CAS) that was issued 7 months ago. A CAS is only valid for 6 months from the date it was assigned to you by your university. You will need to ask your university to issue a new CAS before you can apply for your visa.

question: Can I do freelance work for my own clients while I'm on a Student visa?
expected: No, you cannot be self-employed on a Student visa

rag.answer: No, you cannot do freelance work for your own clients on a Student visa because you cannot be self-employed [1].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview > What you can and cannot do

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot do freelance work or engage in business for your own clients while on a Student visa. UK Student visa holders are strictly prohibited from being self-employed, running a business, or providing freelance services. Doing so would be a serious breach of your visa conditions.

question: How long can I stay in the UK with a Graduate visa?
expected: 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027, or 3 years with a PhD

rag.answer: A Graduate visa lasts for 3 years if you completed a PhD or other doctoral qualification [1, 2]. For other eligible courses, it lasts for 2 years if you apply on or before 31 December 2026, or 18 months if you apply on or after 1 January 2027 [1, 2].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Overview > How long you can stay
Graduate visa > Overview > How long you can stay

closed_book.answer: You can stay in the UK for up to 2 years with a Graduate visa. However, if you have a PhD or other doctoral qualification, you can stay for up to 3 years. The visa cannot be extended, and you must switch to another visa if you want to stay longer.

question: What's the fee for a Graduate visa?
expected: £937, plus the healthcare surcharge (usually £1,035 a year)

rag.answer: To apply for a Graduate visa, you must pay the £937 application fee [1, 2]. You will also need to pay the healthcare surcharge, which is usually £1,035 for each year you spend in the UK [1, 2].

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > How much it costs
Graduate visa > How much it costs

closed_book.answer: The application fee for a Graduate visa is £822. You must also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge for the full length of time your visa will be valid.

question: Can I extend my Graduate visa when it runs out?
expected: No, it cannot be extended, but you may be able to switch to another visa such as Skilled Worker

rag.answer: No, you cannot extend your Graduate visa [1]. However, you may be able to switch to a different type of visa, such as a Skilled Worker visa [1].

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > How long you can stay

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot extend a Graduate visa. It is a non-renewable visa that is only granted once for a maximum of 2 years (or 3 years for PhD graduates). Once it expires, you must switch to another visa route, such as a Skilled Worker visa, if you wish to stay in the UK.

question: Do I have to wait for my graduation ceremony before I apply for the Graduate visa?
expected: No, you can apply once your university has told the Home Office you've completed the course, as long as your Student visa hasn't expired

rag.answer: No, you do not have to wait until you have graduated or have been given a certificate [1]. You can apply after your education provider has told the Home Office that you have successfully completed the course you took with your Student or Tier 4 (General) student visa [1].

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > When to apply

closed_book.answer: No, you do not have to wait for your graduation ceremony to apply for the Graduate visa. You only need to wait until your UK higher education provider has officially confirmed to the Home Office that you have successfully completed your course.

question: My master's was one year long and I went home over Christmas. Does that still count as studying in the UK for the Graduate visa?
expected: Yes, leaving during term breaks or weekends still counts; you need to have studied in the UK for the full length of a course of 12 months or less

rag.answer: Yes, leaving the UK during term breaks, such as over Christmas, still counts as time spent studying in the UK [1]. For a master's degree, you need to have studied in the UK for at least 12 months (or the total length of your course) [1], but short absences like term breaks do not interrupt this [1].

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > The course you studied > How long you studied in the UK for

closed_book.answer: Yes, your time away over Christmas still counts as studying in the UK for the Graduate visa. To be eligible, you must have studied a UK bachelor’s degree, master’s degree, or other eligible qualification for at least 12 months (or the full duration of your course if it is shorter) while lawfully in the UK on a valid student visa. Short, permitted absences during your studies, such as holidays or Christmas breaks, do not break this requirement.

question: Can I start my own company while I'm on a Graduate visa?
expected: Yes, you can be self-employed on a Graduate visa

rag.answer: Yes, you can be self-employed while you are on a Graduate visa [2].

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > What you can and cannot do

closed_book.answer: Yes, you can start your own company while you are on a Graduate visa. The Graduate visa allows you to be self-employed and engage in business, provided you meet the general conditions of the visa. However, you cannot work as a professional sportsperson or sports coach.

question: Can I go home for a holiday while my Graduate visa application is being processed?
expected: No, if you leave the UK, Ireland, the Channel Islands or the Isle of Man before a decision, your application is withdrawn

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: No, you must not travel outside the UK, Ireland, the Channel Islands, or the Isle of Man while your Graduate visa application is pending. If you leave the Common Travel Area while your application is being processed, your application will be withdrawn.

question: What English test score do I need for a Skilled Worker visa?
expected: At least CEFR level B2 (B1 if you had the visa before 8 January 2026 and are extending or updating it)

rag.answer: For a Skilled Worker visa, you must generally prove your English skills to at least level B2 on the CEFR scale by passing a Secure English Language Test (SELT) if you do not have other qualifying qualifications [1, 2, 3]. However, if you had a Skilled Worker visa before 8 January 2026 and are applying to extend or update it, you only need level B1 English [1].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Knowledge of English > Passing an English test
Skilled Worker visa > Knowledge of English
Skilled Worker visa > Overview > Eligibility

closed_book.answer: To get a Skilled Worker visa, you must prove your knowledge of the English language by passing a Secure English Language Test (SELT) from an approved provider. You will need to achieve at least level B1 on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) scale in reading, writing, listening, and speaking. You do not need to take a test if you are a national of a majority English-speaking country or if you have a degree taught in English that is recognised by Ecctis as equivalent to a UK bachelor's degree.

question: How much savings do I need to show for a Skilled Worker visa?
expected: £1,270, held for 28 days in a row, unless you've been in the UK for 12 months or your employer covers your first month's costs

rag.answer:
You will usually need to have at least £1,270 available in your bank account to support yourself [1, 2]. This money must have been available to you for at least 28 days in a row, with day 28 falling within 31 days of your application [2]. 

However, you do not need to show this proof if you have been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months, or if your employer covers your costs up to £1,270 during your first month [2].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > How much it costs
Skilled Worker visa > How much it costs > Money to support yourself

closed_book.answer: You generally need to have at least £1,270 in your bank account to show you can support yourself when applying for a Skilled Worker visa. The money must have been available for at least 30 consecutive days, ending no more than 31 days before the date you submit your application. However, you may be exempt from this requirement if your employer is an A-rated sponsor who agrees to cover your costs (certify your maintenance) during your first month in the UK.

question: If I apply for a Skilled Worker visa from India, how long until I hear back?
expected: Usually within 3 weeks

rag.answer: If you apply for a Skilled Worker visa from outside the UK (such as from India), you will usually get a decision within 3 weeks after you have applied online, proved your identity, and provided your documents [1]. Your application may take longer if your documents need to be verified, you need to attend an interview, or because of personal circumstances like a criminal conviction [1]. You may also have the option to pay for a faster decision [1].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Apply from outside the UK > How long it takes to get a decision

closed_book.answer: If you apply for a Skilled Worker visa from outside the UK, including from India, you will usually get a decision within 3 weeks. You may be able to pay for a faster service, such as a priority or super priority visa, to get a decision sooner depending on the options available at your visa application centre.

question: Can I have a weekend job on top of my sponsored job?
expected: Yes, up to 20 hours a week if the job meets the conditions (e.g. higher skilled, on the immigration salary list, or same sector and level); more than that needs a visa update

rag.answer: Yes, you can work up to 20 hours a week in another job as long as you continue doing the job you are sponsored for, provided the additional work meets certain conditions like being higher skilled, on the immigration salary list, or in the same sector and level as your main job [1]. If your weekend job is more than 20 paid hours a week, you must apply to update your visa to include both jobs [3].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Taking on additional work > Working in another job or for your own business
Skilled Worker visa > Update your visa if you change job or employer > Eligibility and documents you’ll need to apply

closed_book.answer: Yes, you can take a second job on a Skilled Worker visa, but it must meet certain conditions. The extra job must be for up to 20 hours a week, and it must either be in an eligible occupation code or on the Immigration Salary List. Additionally, your second job must take place outside of your contracted working hours for your main sponsored job. You do not need to update your visa, but your main sponsor must remain your primary employer.

question: A different company offered me a job. Can I just move there on my Skilled Worker visa?
expected: No, you must apply to update your visa first (up to 3 months before the new job starts) and should not start until it's approved

rag.answer: You need to apply to update your Skilled Worker visa if you change your job and your new job is with a different employer [1]. Therefore, you cannot just move to the new company without updating your visa.

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Update your visa if you change job or employer

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot just move to a new employer on your existing Skilled Worker visa. Your new employer must be a licensed sponsor and issue you a new Certificate of Sponsorship (CoS). You must then submit a new visa application to update your visa with your new job details before you can start working for them.

question: After how many years on a Skilled Worker visa can I get permanent residency?
expected: After 5 years you may be able to apply for indefinite leave to remain

rag.answer: After 5 years on a Skilled Worker visa, you may be able to apply to settle permanently in the UK, which is also known as indefinite leave to remain [1].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Overview > How long you can stay

closed_book.answer:
You can usually apply for permanent residency, known as indefinite leave to remain, after living and working in the UK for 5 years on a Skilled Worker visa. You must continue to meet the salary and job requirements, and not have spent too many days outside the UK. 

I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

question: How much money does my wife need to show to join me on my Skilled Worker visa?
expected: £285 for a partner, held for 28 days in a row

rag.answer: Your partner will need to have £285 available to support herself in the UK [3]. You or your partner will need to have had this money available for at least 28 days in a row, with day 28 falling within 31 days of applying for the visa [3]. She will not need to show proof of this money if you have all been in the UK with a valid visa for at least 12 months, or if your employer can cover your family's costs during the first month and this is confirmed on your certificate of sponsorship [3].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Your partner and children > Money they need to support themselves

closed_book.answer: To bring your wife to the UK as your dependant on a Skilled Worker visa, she generally needs to show £285 for her own funds. You will also need to show additional funds for any other dependants joining you: £315 for the first child and £200 for each additional child. These funds must be held in a bank account for at least 28 consecutive days, ending no more than 31 days before the date of the application.

question: I'm starting a one-year taught master's in September. Can my wife come with me?
expected: Usually no: postgraduate courses starting on or after 1 January 2024 must be a PhD or research degree, unless you're a government-sponsored student on a course longer than 6 months

rag.answer: No, your wife cannot come with you as your dependant [1]. To bring a partner on a Student visa, you must be either a government-sponsored student on a course lasting over 6 months, or a full-time student on a postgraduate level course lasting 9 months or longer that is either a PhD, another doctorate, or a research-based higher degree [1]. A taught master's degree does not meet these specific dependant requirements [1].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Your partner and children

closed_book.answer: Generally, as a student starting a postgraduate taught course that lasts for 9 months or longer starting before 1 January 2024, your dependents (such as your wife) can apply to join you. However, if your course starts on or after 1 January 2024, international students on taught master's courses are generally no longer allowed to bring dependants to the UK.

question: What's the minimum salary I need to get a Skilled Worker visa?
expected: £41,700 a year or the going rate for the job, whichever is higher (lower in some cases)

rag.answer:
To get a Skilled Worker visa, you must generally be paid at least £41,700 per year or the ‘going rate’ for your type of work, whichever is highest [1]. 

However, lower minimum salaries may apply depending on your circumstances [1]. For example, if you are extending your visa, updating it due to a new job or employer, or switching to become a prison officer [1]. You might also be paid less (at least £33,400 per year) if you are under 26, studying, a recent graduate, in professional training, have a relevant STEM PhD, or hold a postdoctoral position [2, 3].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > Your job
Skilled Worker visa > Your job > Salary requirements
Skilled Worker visa > When you can be paid less

closed_book.answer:
Generally, the minimum general salary requirement for a Skilled Worker visa is £38,700 per year, or the going rate for your specific occupation, whichever is higher. However, you may be able to be paid less (known as a "discount") if you meet certain criteria, such as having a PhD relevant to your job, working in a shortage occupation, or being a new entrant to the job market. 

I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have regarding the exact lower salary thresholds for those eligible for discounts, as these vary by specific circumstance and occupation code.

question: If I apply for my Graduate visa in February 2027, how long will it last?
expected: 18 months (3 years with a PhD)

rag.answer: If you apply for your Graduate visa in February 2027 (which is on or after 1 January 2027), your visa will last for 18 months [1]. However, if you have completed a PhD or other doctoral qualification, your Graduate visa will last for 3 years [1].

citations.title_path: Graduate visa > Overview > How long you can stay

closed_book.answer: If you apply for a Graduate visa, it will typically last for 2 years. However, if your eligible qualification is a PhD or other doctoral qualification, the visa will last for 3 years.

question: I'm on a Graduate visa. Can a company sponsor me for a Skilled Worker job that pays less than the normal minimum?
expected: Yes, you can be paid 70% of the going rate if it's at least £33,400 a year, but your total stay (including Graduate visa time) cannot exceed 4 years

rag.answer: Yes, you might still be able to apply for a Skilled Worker visa if your salary is less than the standard requirement, provided your job is eligible [1]. Because you are a recent graduate, you can be paid between 70% and 90% of the standard going rate if your salary is at least £33,400 per year [1]. Specifically, you can be paid 70% of the standard going rate if you meet criteria such as being under 26 on the date you apply, or having been in the UK on a Graduate visa in the last 2 years (where a Graduate or visit visa was your most recent visa) [3]. However, your total stay in the UK cannot be more than 4 years if you apply for this reason [3].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > When you can be paid less
Skilled Worker visa > When you can be paid less > You’re under 26, studying or a recent graduate, or in professional training

closed_book.answer: Yes, a company can sometimes sponsor you for a Skilled Worker job that pays less than the normal general salary threshold, provided you meet certain criteria such as being under 26, a recent graduate, or applying for a job on the Immigration Salary List. However, the salary must still meet at least 70% to 90% of the usual going rate for that specific occupation, depending on the exact discount category you qualify for.

question: What will a 2-year Skilled Worker visa cost me in total if I apply from abroad?
expected: £819 application fee plus £1,035 a year healthcare surcharge, £2,889 in total, plus £1,270 savings unless your employer covers it (lower fee if the job is on the immigration salary list)

rag.answer: When you apply for a 2-year Skilled Worker visa from abroad for a job that is not on the immigration salary list, the standard application fee is £819 [1]. You will also need to pay the healthcare surcharge of £1,035 for each year of your stay, which equals £2,070 for 2 years [1]. Additionally, unless you are exempt or your employer covers the costs, you must prove you have at least £1,270 available to support yourself [1].

citations.title_path: Skilled Worker visa > How much it costs

closed_book.answer: If you apply for a 2-year Skilled Worker visa from outside the UK, the standard application fee is £719 if your job is on the Immigration Salary List, or £1,420 for most other jobs. You must also pay the Immigration Health Surcharge, which is £1,035 per year (£2,070 in total for 2 years). Additionally, you must meet the financial requirement of having at least £1,270 in available funds, unless you are exempt.

question: Can I switch from my Student visa to a Skilled Worker visa before I finish my course?
expected: Only if your job starts after the course ends, or you're a full-time PhD student who has studied for at least 24 months; otherwise you must complete the course first

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: Yes, you can switch from a Student visa to a Skilled Worker visa before you finish your course, provided you meet certain conditions. You must have completed your studies, or your start date with your employer must be after your course completion date. Additionally, your sponsoring employer must be a licensed sponsor with a valid Certificate of Sponsorship, and the job must meet the relevant skill and salary requirements.

question: I'm from Malaysia. Do I need to show bank statements for my Student visa?
expected: Usually not, Malaysia is on the differential evidence list, but you might still be asked for it before a decision

rag.answer: Because you are from Malaysia, you do not need to prove you have enough money to support yourself for your Student visa [1]. However, you might still be asked to provide this evidence before a decision is made on your application [1]. If UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) requires you to provide it, they will contact you after you submit your application [1].

citations.title_path: Student visa > Money you need > When you do not need to prove you have money to support yourself

closed_book.answer: Whether you need to show bank statements for a UK Student visa depends on your circumstances. If you are a national of Malaysia and applying under the differential evidence requirement, you usually do not need to submit financial documents with your application, though the Home Office reserves the right to request them. If you do not qualify for this requirement, you must provide bank statements showing you hold the required funds for tuition fees and living costs.

question: Can I apply for British citizenship straight after my Graduate visa?
expected: Not covered by these guides

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: No, you cannot apply for British citizenship straight after a Graduate visa because the time spent on a Graduate visa does not count towards the continuous residence requirement for naturalisation. You must first switch to a visa that leads to settlement, such as a Skilled Worker visa, and live in the UK for a specific qualifying period. Generally, you must hold indefinite leave to remain (settlement) for 12 months before you can apply for citizenship, or be married to a British citizen.

question: How many hours a week can I work during term time on a Student visa?
expected: Not covered: the guides only say it depends on the course and whether it's term time, without giving a number

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: If you are studying a full-time degree-level course, you can usually work up to 20 hours a week during term time. If you are studying a course below degree level, you are generally allowed to work up to 10 hours a week during term time. The exact number of hours you are permitted to work will be stated on your biometric residence permit (BRP) or digital immigration status.

question: How do my parents apply for a visitor visa to come to my graduation?
expected: Not covered by these guides

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: Your parents must apply online for a Standard Visitor visa from outside the UK before they travel. They will need to complete the online application form, pay the visa fee, and book an appointment at a visa application centre to submit their fingerprints and photograph. As part of their application, they should provide a valid passport, proof of their finances, and a letter from your university confirming your graduation date and details.

question: How do I get a National Insurance number?
expected: Not covered by these guides

rag.answer: I can't find this in the gov.uk guidance I have.

closed_book.answer: You can apply for a National Insurance number online if you live in the UK, are aged 16 or over, and have the right to work or study here. To apply, you will need to prove your identity using documents like your passport, biometric residence permit, or national identity card. The online application asks for your personal details and employment status, and you will usually receive your number by post within a few weeks.
